title: Distilling universal machine-learning potentials for moiré lattices across one million atoms
authors: Thomas Huang, Yueyao Fan, Kaichen Xie, Bolun Li, Kaijie Yang, Jenna A. Bilbrey, Eric Bylaska, Peter V. Sushko, Di Xiao, Ting Cao
abstract: Atomic reconstruction reshapes moiré materials across multiple scales, from local structure and polarization textures to global electronic topology, yet direct \textit{ab initio} modeling becomes prohibitive for large superstructures such as marginal-twist-angle moirés and moiré-of-moirés. We develop MoiréMLIP by fine-tuning a universal atomistic model on the density functional theory labeled Moiré Kaleidoscope dataset, which spans transition metal dichalcogenide compositions, symmetries, stackings, and twist angles. MoiréMLIP reproduces \textit{ab initio} reconstruction with force errors of 6--8\,meV/Å and transfers to smaller twist angles and unseen structures. Knowledge distillation yields MoiréMLIP-mini, which retains this accuracy while extending single-GPU inference to one million atoms. Applied to an alternate-twist MoTe$_2$ trilayer, it reveals a hierarchical polarization network spanning tens of nanometers arising from large moiré-cell distortions sharply localized along the moiré-of-moiré domain walls. These results overcome key accuracy, transferability, and scaling bottlenecks of existing atomistic models and enable predictive simulations across emergent moiré length scales.
summary: This work introduces MoiréMLIP, a machine-learned potential trained specifically on moiré materials to overcome the computational barriers of simulating large, twisted superstructures. By fine-tuning and compressing this model, the authors created a highly accurate potential capable of simulating systems up to one million atoms. This enables predictive simulations of complex phenomena, such as hierarchical polarization networks, in emergent moiré systems.
main_problem: Direct ab initio modeling of large, complex moiré superstructures is computationally prohibitive due to the high dimensionality of structural degrees of freedom.
main_result: The authors developed MoiréMLIP, a fine-tuned machine-learning potential, which accurately reproduces DFT reconstructions and scales to one million atoms using knowledge distillation.
method: They fine-tuned a universal MLIP on a specialized dataset (Moiré Kaleidoscope) and employed knowledge distillation to create a highly accurate, yet computationally efficient, student model.
model_or_system: The study focuses on moiré lattices formed by twisted transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) like MoTe2. The model aims to capture complex structural reconstructions arising from moiré supercells.
key_observables: Force Root-Mean-Square Error (RMSE), interlayer distance differences (e.g., $\Delta d_{	ext{MM}-	ext{MX}}$), and the emergent polarization network.
important_parameters: Twist angles (e.g., 7.34$^\circ$, 5.09$^\circ$, 3.48$^\circ$), system size (up to one million atoms), and force error thresholds (e.g., 6--8 meV/Å).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that fine-tuning a universal MLIP on a comprehensive dataset can overcome the limitations of existing potentials when applied to novel moiré geometries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow of dataset construction, the learning curves showing force RMSE reduction with training data volume, and the comparison of reconstruction profiles across different models.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the computational bottleneck of moiré materials, introduces the MoiréMLIP methodology via dataset curation and fine-tuning, validates its accuracy against DFT benchmarks, and finally applies the model to predict emergent physical properties like polarization in large-scale systems.
why_interesting: The development of highly accurate, scalable MLIPs for moiré systems provides a powerful tool for simulating emergent electronic and structural phenomena in 2D materials, which is crucial for understanding correlated electron physics in these systems.
